Yes, I usually wear a watch.

I think it's useful to have one so I can see the time easily.

Also, I like the way it looks on my wrist; it's like a simple accessory.

However, sometimes I forget to wear it, especially on weekends.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, yes, I wear a watch pretty much every day. I've sort of got into the habit of it, and I feel a bit lost without one on my wrist. vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you usually wear a watch?
idioms: Time and tide wait for no man - "Vaqt va to'lqin hech kimni kutmaydi"
around the clock - "kechayu kunduz"
in the nick of time - "oxirgi daqiqada"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I actually wear a watch every day..." - "Ha, men aslida har kuni soat taqaman..."
"I prefer wearing a classic analogue watch because..." - "Men klassik analog soat taqishni afzal ko'raman, chunki..."
"Moreover, I see my watch as a..." - "Bundan tashqari, men soatimni ... sifatida ko'raman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I actually wear a watch every day. It's become such a daily habit that I feel incomplete without it on my wrist.
I prefer wearing a classic analogue watch because I think it looks more elegant and professional. Even though I have a phone that tells the time, glancing at my watch is much quicker and more discreet, especially during meetings or classes.
Moreover, I see my watch as a fashion accessory that complements my outfit. As they say, "Time and tide wait for no man", so having a watch is a good reminder to make the most of every moment.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men har kuni soat taqaman. Bu shunchalik kundalik odatga aylanib qolganki, bilagimda soat bo'lmasa o'zimni to'liq his qilmayman.

Men klassik analog soat taqishni afzal ko'raman, chunki u yanada nafis va professional ko'rinadi deb o'ylayman. Garchi telefonda vaqtni ko'rish imkoniyati bo'lsa ham, soatga bir qarash ancha tezroq va ehtiyotkorroq, ayniqsa yig'ilishlar yoki darslar paytida.

Bundan tashqari, men soatimni kiyimimga mos keladigan moda aksessuari sifatida ko'raman. Aytishlaricha, "Vaqt hech kimni kutmaydi", shuning uchun soatning bo'lishi har bir daqiqadan unumli foydalanish uchun yaxshi eslatma bo'ladi.

questions.prompt: Have you ever grown a plant or a flower?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I have a plant. It is green.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I have. I grew a flower. It was red and yellow. It was very small, but it was nice.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I have grown plants. I grew some herbs, like mint. It was in a pot on my windowsill. I think it's quite easy to grow herbs. However, I forgot to water it sometimes, so it died.
questions.sampleB2: Yes, actually, I have, though I'm no expert. Recently I had a go at bringing on some herbs — basil and mint — on my windowsill. To be honest, it was a bit hit and miss: the mint took off nicely, but the basil didn't make it because I kept forgetting to water it. Still, watching something come up from a seed is oddly satisfying.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Menda bir o‘simlik bor. U yashil rangda.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men o'stirganman. Men gul o'stirdim. U qizil va sariq rangda edi. U juda kichkina edi, lekin u yoqimli edi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men o'simliklar o'stirdim. Men yalpiz kabi ba'zi o'tlar o'stirdim. U derazam tokchasidagi tuvakda edi. Menimcha, o'tlar o'stirish juda oson.
Biroq, ba'zan uni sug'orishni unutib qo'yardim, shuning uchun u o'ldi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, men bir necha marta o'simliklar o'stirishga harakat qilganman, muvaffaqiyat darajalari har xil bo'lgan. Bir marta kungaboqar o'stirishga urinishim esimda, bu ancha ulkan maqsad edi. Men ularni unib chiqishiga erishdim, lekin ular hech qachon yaxshi rivojlanmadi, ehtimol, ularga yetarli joyim bo'lmagani uchun. Bu biroz umidsizlikka sabab bo'ldi, lekin men baribir shahar bog'dorchiligining qiyinchiliklari haqida nimadir o'rgandim.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Have you ever grown a plant or a flower?
idioms: To plant a garden is to believe in tomorrow - "Bog' ekish - ertangi kunga ishonish"
nip it in the bud - "boshidanoq oldini olmoq"
come up roses - "hammasi yaxshi tugamoq"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I have! A few years ago, I actually tried..." - "Ha, bor! Bir necha yil oldin men ... ni sinab ko'rdim"
"I particularly enjoyed watching the plants grow..." - "Men ayniqsa o'simliklarning o'sishini kuzatishni yoqtirdim..."
"Unfortunately, I don't have much time for..." - "Afsuski, ... uchun ko'p vaqtim yo'q"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I have! A few years ago, I actually tried growing tomatoes and basil on my balcony. It was a really rewarding experience.
I particularly enjoyed watching the plants grow from tiny seeds into something I could actually use in cooking. It taught me a lot about patience and the importance of consistent care — watering them regularly and making sure they got enough sunlight.
Unfortunately, I don't have much time for gardening these days, but I'd love to take it up again in the future. As they say, "To plant a garden is to believe in tomorrow".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men qilib ko'rganman! Bir necha yil oldin, men balkonimda pomidor va rayhon yetishtirishga harakat qilganman. Bu juda foydali tajriba edi.

Men ayniqsa o'simliklarning kichkina urug'lardan o'sib, ovqat tayyorlashda ishlatishim mumkin bo'lgan narsaga aylanishini kuzatishdan zavqlanardim. Bu menga sabr-toqat va doimiy g'amxo'rlikning muhimligini o'rgatdi — ularni muntazam ravishda sug'orish va yetarli quyosh nurini olishlarini ta'minlash.

Afsuski, hozirgi kunda bog'dorchilikka vaqtim yo'q, lekin kelajakda yana bunga qaytishni xohlardim. Aytishlaricha, "Bog' ekish - ertangi kunga ishonish demakdir".

questions.prompt: Do you smile often in your daily life?
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I smile. I smile when I am happy. And I smile when I see my friends. I like to smile.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I think I smile quite a lot. I'm usually in a good mood, and I like to smile at people. For example, I smile at my colleagues at work. I think it's important to be friendly. Also, it makes me feel good.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, I'd say I do, actually. I suppose I'm quite an upbeat person by nature, so smiling comes naturally to me. The thing is, a smile really can brighten up someone's day — whether it's the barista or a random stranger. It also makes you seem far more approachable. That said, we all have off days when I just put on a brave face.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men kulaman. Men xursand bo'lganimda kulaman. Va do'stlarimni ko'rganimda kulaman. Kulishni yaxshi ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, menimcha, men juda ko'p kulaman. Odatda kayfiyatim yaxshi bo'ladi va odamlarga kulishni yaxshi ko'raman.
Masalan, men ishda hamkasblarimga kulaman. O'ylaymanki, do'stona bo'lish muhim. Bundan tashqari, bu meni yaxshi his qiladi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Menimcha, men yetarlicha tez-tez tabassum qilaman, ha. Tabassum qilish nafaqat o'zimning farovonligim uchun, balki boshqalar bilan qanday munosabatda bo'lishim uchun ham muhim deb hisoblayman. Misol uchun, men kun davomida uchrashadigan odamlarga, supermarketdagi kassirmi yoki qo'shnimmi, tabassum qilishga ongli ravishda harakat qilaman. Bu ularning kuniga, shuningdek, mening kunimga ham kichik, lekin ijobiy ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin. Albatta, ba'zida kayfiyatim bo'lmaydi, lekin odatda, men ijobiy va tabassumli xulq-atvorni saqlashga harakat qilaman.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you smile often in your daily life?
idioms: A smile is the universal welcome - "Tabassum - bu umumjahon salomlashish"
grin from ear to ear - "quloqdan quloqqa tirjaymoq"
laughter is the best medicine - "kulgi eng yaxshi davo"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I'd say I smile quite often..." - "Ha, men kundalik hayotimda tez-tez kulaman..."
"I especially smile when I'm spending time with..." - "Men ayniqsa ... bilan vaqt o'tkazganimda kulaman"
"I also think smiling is incredibly important in..." - "Shuningdek, kulish ... da juda muhim deb o'ylayman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I'd say I smile quite often throughout the day. I'm generally a cheerful person, and I believe that smiling can brighten up not only my own mood but also the people around me.
I especially smile when I'm spending time with friends or family, or when something funny happens unexpectedly. Even small things like a kind message or a beautiful sunset can bring a genuine smile to my face.
I also think smiling is incredibly important in social situations — it makes you appear more approachable and friendly. As they say, "A smile is the universal welcome".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men kun davomida juda ko'p tabassum qilaman deb ayta olaman. Men odatda quvnoq odamman va ishonamanki, tabassum nafaqat o'zimning kayfiyatimni, balki atrofimdagi odamlarning ham kayfiyatini ko'tarishi mumkin.

Men ayniqsa do'stlarim yoki oilam bilan vaqt o'tkazganimda yoki kutilmaganda kulgili bir narsa sodir bo'lganda tabassum qilaman. Hatto mehribon xabar yoki chiroyli quyosh botishi kabi kichik narsalar ham yuzimga chinakam tabassum olib kelishi mumkin.

Menimcha, tabassum ijtimoiy vaziyatlarda juda muhim - bu sizni yanada yaqin va do'stona ko'rsatadi. Aytishlaricha, "Tabassum - bu universal xush kelibsiz".

questions.sampleB2: These two pictures showcase quite different environments and activities. The first image features two professionals, a man and a woman, standing in what looks like a high-tech factory or lab. They are surrounded by robotic arms and holographic displays, suggesting they're discussing advanced technology or industrial processes. The man holds a laptop, while the woman attentively listens. In stark contrast, the second picture presents a single artisan engrossed in his craft. He's shaping a clay pot on a pottery wheel in a traditional workshop. While the first scene emphasizes innovation and digital collaboration, the second highlights manual craftsmanship and traditional skills.

Rasmlarda men narsalarni yasashning ikki xil usulini ko'rishim mumkin.

questions.uzSampleB2:
Rasmlarda ishlab chiqarishga zid yondashuvlar tasvirlangan.

Birinchisi, ehtimol, avtomatlashtirilgan jarayonlar bilan ommaviy ishlab chiqarishga qaratilgan yirik sanoat fabrikasi bo'lib ko'rinadi.

Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda qo'l mehnati bilan shug'ullanayotgan hunarmand tasvirlangan, bu esa yanada hunarmandchilik va individuallashtirilgan yondashuvni taklif qiladi.

Fabrika, ehtimol, samaradorlik va hajmga ustuvor ahamiyat bersa, qo'lda yasalgan buyum, ehtimol, o'ziga xoslik va tafsilotlarga e'tibor berishni ta'kidlaydi.

Narx, sifat va atrof-muhitga ta'siri nuqtai nazaridan ushbu ikki usul o'rtasidagi murosaga kelishuvlarni ko'rib chiqish qiziq.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: cut from the same cloth - "bir xil bo'lmoq"

quality over quantity - "miqdordan ko'ra sifat"
sentenceStarters: "These two pictures present a striking contrast between..." - "Bu ikki rasm ... o'rtasidagi keskin farqni ko'rsatadi"
"In the first picture, I can see..." - "Birinchi rasmda men ... ko'ryapman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
These two pictures present a striking contrast between two very different methods of producing goods.
In the first picture, I can see a large factory or production facility where goods are being manufactured on a massive scale. Everything appears to be automated and highly efficient, with identical products being produced in large quantities on an assembly line.
The second picture shows a very different scene — a craftsperson carefully making items by hand. This represents a more traditional, artisanal approach where each product is unique and made with personal attention and skill. The atmosphere feels much more intimate and creative.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki rasm tovarlar ishlab chiqarishning ikki xil usuli o'rtasida ajoyib kontrastni taqdim etadi.

Birinchi rasmda men katta zavod yoki ishlab chiqarish korxonasini ko'rishim mumkin, u yerda tovarlar keng miqyosda ishlab chiqarilmoqda. Hamma narsa avtomatlashtirilgan va juda samarali ko'rinadi, bir xil mahsulotlar konveyerda katta miqdorda ishlab chiqarilmoqda.

Ikkinchi rasmda butunlay boshqacha manzara aks etgan - hunarmand buyumlarni ehtiyotkorlik bilan qo'lda yasamoqda. Bu an'anaviyroq, hunarmandchilik yondashuvini ifodalaydi, bunda har bir mahsulot noyob va shaxsiy e'tibor va mahorat bilan yaratiladi. Atmosfera ancha samimiy va ijodiy tuyuladi.

questions.prompt: What are the advantages of buying factory-made, mass-produced goods?
questions.sampleA1: I like it. It is cheap. I can buy it.
questions.sampleA2: It is cheaper. And, it is easy to find in the shops. I like that because it is simple.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think the main advantage is the price. Mass-produced things are usually cheaper than handmade things. Also, you can find them everywhere, in many shops. For example, if you need a new shirt, it's very easy to buy one that's made in a factory.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the most obvious one has to be the price. Because everything's churned out on a massive scale, the cost per item comes down dramatically, so it's far more affordable for ordinary people. On top of that, you get real consistency — every unit is identical — and they're readily available in shops everywhere, so replacing something is never a hassle.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga yoqadi. U arzon. Men uni sotib olishim mumkin.
questions.uzSampleA2: U arzonroq. Va, uni do'konlarda topish oson. Menga shu yoqadi, chunki u oddiy.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, menimcha, asosiy afzalligi narxidir. Ommaviy ishlab chiqarilgan narsalar odatda qo'lda yasalgan narsalardan arzonroq bo'ladi. Bundan tashqari, ularni hamma joyda, ko'plab do'konlarda topishingiz mumkin. Masalan, agar sizga yangi ko'ylak kerak bo'lsa, fabrikada ishlab chiqarilganini sotib olish juda oson.
questions.uzSampleB2: Bitta aniq afzalligi bu narx. Ommaviy ishlab chiqarilgan mahsulotlar, odatda, miqyos iqtisodiyoti tufayli arzonroq bo'ladi. Shuningdek, mavjudligi katta plyus. Siz bu mahsulotlarni ko'pchilik do'konlarda osongina topishingiz mumkin va ular ko'pincha osonlik bilan almashtiriladi. Bundan tashqari, siz kutishingiz mumkin bo'lgan ma'lum bir darajadagi izchillik mavjud, bu ba'zi iste'molchilar uchun ishonchli bo'lishi mumkin, hatto bu o'ziga xoslikdan voz kechishni anglatsa ham.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the advantages of buying factory-made, mass-produced goods?
idioms: Necessity is the mother of invention - "Ehtiyoj - ixtironing onasi"
get your money's worth - "pulingga yarasha narsa olmoq"
a dime a dozen - "juda arzon va ko'p"
sentenceStarters: "There are several significant advantages to..." - "... ning bir nechta muhim afzalliklari bor"
"Firstly, mass-produced items are generally much more..." - "Birinchidan, ommaviy ishlab chiqarilgan mahsulotlar odatda ..."
"Additionally, mass production allows for..." - "Bundan tashqari, ommaviy ishlab chiqarish ... imkonini beradi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several significant advantages to buying factory-made, mass-produced goods, as illustrated in the first picture.
Firstly, mass-produced items are generally much more affordable than handmade products. Because factories produce goods in large quantities, the cost per unit is significantly lower, making them accessible to a wider range of consumers.
Secondly, factory-made goods offer consistency and reliability. Every product coming off the assembly line meets the same quality standards, so customers know exactly what they're getting. There are fewer surprises in terms of quality.
Additionally, mass production allows for greater availability — these products are stocked in stores everywhere and can be replaced easily if something breaks. As they say, "Necessity is the mother of invention", and factories have made essential goods available to millions.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda ko'rsatilganidek, zavodda ishlab chiqarilgan, ommaviy ishlab chiqarilgan mahsulotlarni sotib olishning bir nechta muhim afzalliklari bor.

Birinchidan, ommaviy ishlab chiqarilgan mahsulotlar odatda qo'lda tayyorlangan mahsulotlarga qaraganda ancha arzonroq bo'ladi. Zavodlar mahsulotlarni katta miqdorda ishlab chiqarishi sababli, har bir birlikning narxi sezilarli darajada past bo'ladi, bu ularni iste'molchilarning keng doirasi uchun ochiq qiladi.

Ikkinchidan, zavodda ishlab chiqarilgan mahsulotlar izchillik va ishonchlilikni ta'minlaydi. Konveyerdan chiqadigan har bir mahsulot bir xil sifat standartlariga javob beradi, shuning uchun mijozlar nima olayotganini aniq bilishadi. Sifat jihatidan kutilmagan hodisalar kamroq bo'ladi.

Bundan tashqari, ommaviy ishlab chiqarish katta mavjudlikni ta'minlaydi — bu mahsulotlar hamma joyda do'konlarda mavjud va agar biror narsa buzilsa, ularni osongina almashtirish mumkin. Aytishlaricha, "Ehtiyoj ixtironing onasi", va zavodlar millionlab odamlar uchun zaruriy mahsulotlarni ta'minladi.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do people often value handmade items, even if they are more expensive?
idioms: The best things in life are worth waiting for - "Hayotdagi eng yaxshi narsalar kutishga arziydi"
blood, sweat, and tears - "qon, ter va ko'z yoshi"
put your heart and soul into something - "biror narsaga jon-dil bilan kirishmoq"
sentenceStarters: "Many people are willing to pay a premium for..." - "Ko'p odamlar ... uchun ko'proq pul to'lashga tayyor"
"Primarily, handmade products are unique and..." - "Birinchi navbatda, qo'lda yasalgan mahsulotlar noyob va..."
"Moreover, many people choose handmade goods because..." - "Bundan tashqari, ko'pchilik qo'lda yasalgan mahsulotlarni tanlaydi, chunki..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Many people are willing to pay a premium for handmade items, as shown in the second picture, and there are several compelling reasons for this.
Primarily, handmade products are unique and one-of-a-kind. Unlike factory goods, each handcrafted item has its own character and small imperfections that make it truly special. People appreciate owning something that nobody else has.
Furthermore, there's a deep appreciation for the skill and craftsmanship involved. When you buy a handmade item, you're paying for hours of dedicated work, years of expertise, and genuine passion. It feels more meaningful than a product made by a machine.
Moreover, many people choose handmade goods because they want to support local artisans and small businesses rather than large corporations. There's also a growing awareness that handmade products are often more environmentally sustainable. As they say, "The best things in life are worth waiting for".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ko'pchilik odamlar qo'lda yasalgan buyumlar uchun qo'shimcha pul to'lashga tayyor, bu ikkinchi rasmda ko'rsatilganidek, va buning bir nechta asosli sabablari bor.

Avvalo, qo'lda yasalgan mahsulotlar noyob va yagona nusxadir. Zavod mahsulotlaridan farqli o'laroq, har bir qo'lda yasalgan buyum o'ziga xos xususiyatga va uni haqiqatan ham maxsus qiladigan kichik kamchiliklarga ega. Odamlar hech kimda yo'q narsaga egalik qilishni qadrlashadi.

Bundan tashqari, bunda ishtirok etgan mahorat va hunarmandchilikka chuqur minnatdorchilik bor. Qo'lda yasalgan buyumni sotib olayotganda, siz soatlab bag'ishlangan mehnat, ko'p yillik tajriba va chinakam ishtiyoq uchun pul to'laysiz. Bu mashina tomonidan ishlab chiqarilgan mahsulotdan ko'ra ko'proq ma'noli tuyuladi.

Bundan tashqari, ko'pchilik odamlar yirik korporatsiyalardan ko'ra mahalliy hunarmandlar va kichik biznesni qo'llab-quvvatlashni xohlashlari sababli qo'lda yasalgan mahsulotlarni tanlashadi. Shuningdek, qo'lda yasalgan mahsulotlar ko'pincha ekologik jihatdan barqaror ekanligi haqida tobora ortib borayotgan xabardorlik mavjud. Aytishlaricha, "Hayotdagi eng yaxshi narsalarni kutishga arziydi".

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you made a big purchase.
questions.sampleA1: I buy a phone. It is new. It is red.
questions.sampleA2: I bought a bike. It was for my birthday. It was expensive, but I like it.
questions.sampleB1: I bought a car last year. It was a big decision because it cost a lot of money. I needed it for my job, though. I think it was a good choice, even if it's expensive to maintain.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so the biggest purchase I've ever made would have to be my first car, which I bought a couple of years ago. To be honest, it was a pretty daunting decision, because it set me back a fair chunk of everything I'd saved up. I spent weeks shopping around, comparing models and weighing up the pros and cons, until I finally settled on a small second-hand hatchback — nothing flashy, but reliable and easy on fuel. Looking back, it was worth every penny, because it gave me so much freedom to get to work and visit family. As for saving money, I'll be honest — I find it genuinely hard. There always seems to be some unexpected expense that eats into my savings just when I think I'm getting ahead, whether it's the car breaking down or a bill I'd forgotten about. The thing that works for me, though, is setting aside a fixed amount the moment I get paid, before I have a chance to fritter it away. Out of sight, out of mind, as they say. And on whether money can buy happiness — well, I suppose it's a bit of a mixed bag. Money can definitely buy comfort and peace of mind, and there's no denying that struggling to make ends meet makes life stressful. That said, I really don't think it's the be-all and end-all. The things that matter most — good health, close relationships, a sense of purpose — you simply can't put a price on those. So my take is that money helps, but it certainly isn't everything.

afzalliklari va kamchiliklarini o'lchab ko'rdim.
Oxir-oqibat, men yaxshi joylashuvda kichikroq joyga qaror qildim. Garchi bu mening byudjetimni cho'zgan bo'lsa ham, bu kelajagim uchun arzirli sarmoya edi.

bulletPoints: Tell me about a time you made a big purchase.
How easy do you find it to save money?
Do you think that money can buy happiness?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A big purchase I made:
One of the biggest purchases I've ever made was buying a new laptop about a year ago. I needed it for my studies and work, and I spent approximately $800, which was a significant amount of money for me. I researched different brands and models for weeks before finally making my decision. It was definitely worth it because it has made my work much more efficient and productive.
Saving money:
To be honest, I find it quite challenging to save money. As a student, my income is limited, and there are always unexpected expenses that eat into my savings. However, I try to follow the rule of setting aside at least 10% of any money I receive. I've found that having a separate savings account helps because the money is out of sight, out of mind.
Can money buy happiness?
This is a fascinating question. I believe money can certainly buy comfort, security, and opportunities, which indirectly contribute to happiness. However, true happiness comes from relationships, health, and a sense of purpose — things that money alone cannot provide. As they say, "Money can't buy happiness, but it can make misery more comfortable".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men qilgan katta xarid:

Men qilgan eng katta xaridlardan biri taxminan bir yil oldin yangi noutbuk sotib olganim bo'lgan. Menga u o'qishim va ishim uchun kerak edi va men taxminan 800 dollar sarfladim, bu men uchun juda katta pul edi. Qaror qabul qilishdan oldin bir necha hafta davomida turli brendlar va modellarni o'rgandim. Bu, albatta, arziydi, chunki u mening ishimni ancha samarali va unumli qildi.

Pul yig'ish:

Rostini aytsam, pul yig'ish men uchun juda qiyin. Talaba sifatida mening daromadim cheklangan va har doim kutilmagan xarajatlar bo'lib, ular jamg'armalarimni yeb bitiradi. Biroq, men olgan har qanday pulning kamida 10 foizini ajratib qo'yish qoidasiga amal qilishga harakat qilaman. Alohida jamg'arma hisob raqamiga ega bo'lish yordam berishini aniqladim, chunki pul ko'zdan g'oyib bo'ladi, dildan ham.

Pul baxt sotib oladimi?

Bu juda qiziqarli savol. Menimcha, pul, albatta, qulaylik, xavfsizlik va imkoniyatlarni sotib olishi mumkin, ular bilvosita baxtga hissa qo'shadi. Biroq, haqiqiy baxt munosabatlar, sog'liq va maqsad tuyg'usidan kelib chiqadi - bularni faqat pul bilan ta'minlab bo'lmaydi. Aytishlaricha, "Pul baxt sotib ololmaydi, lekin u baxtsizlikni yanada qulayroq qilishi mumkin".

questions.prompt: The government is responsible for environmental protection.
questions.sampleA2: I think the government is important for the environment. They can help the trees and the animals. But people also need to help, because it is our world.
questions.sampleB1: I think the government has a big role to play in protecting the environment. They can make laws about pollution and protect forests. For example, they can fine companies that pollute rivers. However, I also think that individuals need to do their part, like recycling and saving energy. It's a shared responsibility, in my opinion.
questions.sampleB2: This is a really important issue, and I think there's a strong case on both sides. On the one hand, you could argue that the government has to take the lead on protecting the environment. For a start, only governments can sit down and negotiate international cooperation — an ordinary person simply can't broker a global climate deal. What's more, they control public spending and taxation, so they can pour money into renewable energy and green infrastructure. And crucially, they have the power to regulate big business and crack down on companies that pollute. On the other hand, plenty of people would say that leaning on the government alone just isn't enough. For one thing, governments tend to change every four years or so, which means policies can be chopped and changed or scrapped altogether. On top of that, real, lasting progress often comes down to collective action — millions of small everyday changes, like cutting waste and recycling, can honestly add up to a massive impact. Personally, I sit somewhere in the middle — I can see the merit in both arguments. I do think the government should set the ball rolling with strong laws and funding, since they've got the reach and the resources that no one else has. But at the end of the day, it has to be a shared responsibility — legislation only really works when ordinary people are willing to do their bit too. As the saying goes, we borrow the earth from our children, so looking after it is on all of us.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, hukumat atrof-muhit uchun muhim. Ular daraxtlar va hayvonlarga yordam berishi mumkin. Lekin odamlar ham yordam berishi kerak, chunki bu bizning dunyomiz.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, hukumat atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilishda katta rol o'ynashi kerak. Ular ifloslanish haqida qonunlar chiqarishi va o'rmonlarni himoya qilishi mumkin.
Masalan, ular daryolarni ifloslantiradigan kompaniyalarni jarimaga tortishi mumkin.
Biroq, menimcha, shaxslar ham o'z hissalarini qo'shishlari kerak, masalan, qayta ishlash va energiyani tejash. Bu, mening fikrimcha, umumiy mas'uliyat.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Hukumat atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilish uchun katta mas'uliyatga ega ekanligi inkor etib bo'lmaydi. Ularda ifloslanish, o'rmonlarning kesilishi va resurslarni boshqarish bo'yicha qonun-qoidalarni qabul qilish va amalga oshirish uchun qonun chiqaruvchi hokimiyat mavjud.
Bundan tashqari, hukumatlar qayta tiklanadigan energiya infratuzilmasiga investitsiya kiritishi va soliq imtiyozlari va subsidiyalar orqali barqaror amaliyotlarni rag'batlantirishi mumkin.
Biroq, faqat hukumat harakatiga tayanish yetarli emas. Shaxsiy mas'uliyat va korporativ javobgarlik ham muhimdir.
Nihoyat, hukumat nazoratini mahalliy tashabbuslar va mas'uliyatli biznes amaliyotlari bilan birlashtirgan ko'p qirrali yondashuv atrof-muhitni samarali muhofaza qilish uchun zarurdir.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a highly important debate, especially given the current state of our environment.
Those who believe the government should be responsible for environmental protection make several compelling points. Firstly, governments have the power to negotiate international cooperation on environmental issues — individual citizens simply cannot arrange global climate agreements. Secondly, the government controls public spending and taxation, meaning they can direct funds towards renewable energy, conservation, and green infrastructure. Additionally, only governments have the authority to regulate big business and enforce environmental laws to prevent pollution and exploitation of natural resources.
However, opponents argue that relying solely on government is not enough. Collective action by individuals and communities often leads to more real and lasting progress. Governments change every few years with new elections, which can lead to inconsistent policies — a new administration might reverse environmental regulations. Furthermore, many believe that small everyday changes by millions of people — like reducing waste, recycling, and choosing sustainable products — make the biggest overall impact.
Personally, I think environmental protection requires a shared responsibility. Governments must lead with strong policies, but real change happens when every individual plays their part. As they say, "We do not inherit the earth from our ancestors, we borrow it from our children".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu juda muhim bahs, ayniqsa hozirgi atrof-muhitimiz holatini hisobga olsak.

Atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilish uchun hukumat mas'ul bo'lishi kerak deb hisoblovchilar bir nechta ishonarli dalillarni keltirishadi. Birinchidan, hukumatlar atrof-muhit masalalari bo'yicha xalqaro hamkorlikni muzokara qilish vakolatiga ega - oddiy fuqarolar global iqlim bo'yicha kelishuvlarni tuzishga qodir emas. Ikkinchidan, hukumat davlat xarajatlari va soliqqa tortishni nazorat qiladi, ya'ni ular mablag'larni qayta tiklanadigan energiya, tabiatni muhofaza qilish va yashil infratuzilmaga yo'naltira oladi. Bundan tashqari, faqat hukumatlar yirik biznesni tartibga solish va ifloslanish hamda tabiiy resurslardan foydalanishning oldini olish uchun atrof-muhit qonunlarini amalga oshirish huquqiga ega.

Biroq, qarshi tomonlar faqat hukumatga tayanish yetarli emasligini ta'kidlaydilar. Jismoniy shaxslar va jamiyatlarning jamoaviy harakatlari ko'pincha yanada real va uzoq muddatli taraqqiyotga olib keladi. Hukumatlar har bir necha yilda yangi saylovlar bilan o'zgaradi, bu esa nomuvofiq siyosatlarga olib kelishi mumkin - yangi ma'muriyat atrof-muhit qoidalarini bekor qilishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ko'pchilik millionlab odamlarning kichik kundalik o'zgarishlari - masalan, chiqindilarni kamaytirish, qayta ishlash va barqaror mahsulotlarni tanlash - eng katta umumiy ta'sir ko'rsatadi deb hisoblaydi.

Shaxsan men, atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilish umumiy mas'uliyatni talab qiladi deb o'ylayman. Hukumatlar kuchli siyosat bilan yetakchilik qilishi kerak, lekin har bir shaxs o'z rolini o'ynaganda haqiqiy o'zgarish sodir bo'ladi. Aytishlaricha, "Biz yerni ota-bobolarimizdan meros qilib olmaymiz, biz uni farzandlarimizdan qarzga olamiz".
